No second reader, doorway or turn kind.

Her answer is a read through the registry (new tool 27 file.pages, Kernel op file.pages, read scope) used through tools.use, so it carries receipts like X3's spending answer; its check verifies the file's digest before and after (it never dispatches the read again, so the ASK turn is never asked twice).

New registry numbers 24 files.list, 25 files.copy, 26 files.trash, 27 file.pages (24 to 30 were free: 1-23 K2/K4, 31-35 K9, 101+ K6). Delete is "to the bin" (files.trash: DELETE keeps it, Restore puts it back), so it is a grantable change like K3's other file operations; nothing unrecoverable is offered.

Home things in the PLAN question are D handles (folder, file, group) appended to the desk only for the question (the desk's own planner never sees them); a group is a deduction from the ends of the names, said as such. A group step is the desk's to expand ("6 D2": the folder made first when missing, then a move per file), so a five-kind tidy fits in five model steps.

The PLAN answer cap went 48 -> 64 for eight steps (the estimate: "25 D7 D1|" is 7 tokens); the 20 s deadline and the request's 25 s ceiling are unchanged; when handles have two digits the grammar keeps as many steps as fit (seven). Measured with the 4B: PLAN priced 18.9 s, answered in 11.8 s and 7.7 s.

After the 4B answered a tidy with the bin for every group, the bin, a copy and a rename are in a question's grammar (and accepted by the desk) only when the owner's own words name them; a step that repeats an earlier one, or moves a file an earlier step moves, is refused. K4's rule (a change only the model chose is offered, never done) still holds for move and new folder.

One press for several grants is a new approve operation (grant.give.set) rather than a change to grant.give: each grant stays its own record (operation, target, scope) with its own words in the digest the owner saw; the set is offered only when the step waiting for a grant shares its folder with pending steps of other operations, so every other plan keeps K3's single press.
